paras: The Omaha teamsters' strike circular was a printed warning issued in June 1919 by Teamsters' Union Local 211 in Omaha, Nebraska, during a strike, claiming that Black strikebreakers were being brought from East St. Louis. The circular urged residents to protect their families and homes and called on a local revolver club to "take notice". The Monitor, Omaha's Black weekly, reprinted it, called the report of strikebreakers false, and accused the union of stirring up prejudice against the race.

In June 1919 Omaha's teamsters were on strike, saying they sought higher wages, though, according to the Monitor, it was claimed that their real aim was a closed shop. The Monitor stated that it accepted the right of labor to organize, opposed the closed shop, and did not intend to judge the merits of the strike.

Headed "Warning to Citizens!", the circular told "law-abiding citizens of Omaha" to protect "their wives and daughters from the horrors of East St. Louis" and to safeguard their homes, valuables and lives. It asked whether readers wanted another "influx of Negroes and disreputable" like the one Omaha had experienced in the summer of 1917. Citing "reliable information", it said a carload of Negroes was again being imported from East St. Louis to break the strike. The text closed with "Prettiest Mile Revolver club, take notice!" and was signed by the union's conference committee.

The Monitor said it had traced the "reliable information" and found it "absolutely false" and manufactured for a purpose, adding that no Black strikebreakers were being imported and that "Mr. Rooney of the Teamsters' Union" knew it. The coverage reports no violence, arrests or official response connected with the circular.

The only report found is an editorial in the Monitor of June 19, 1919, which printed the circular in full beneath an unrelated item nominating Emmett J. Scott for the Spingarn Medal. The paper described the circular as propaganda "evidently intended to create prejudice against the Colored race" and "an adroit appeal to stir up prejudice". While insisting it was not opposed to organized labor "if it does not discriminate," the Monitor pledged to oppose any effort "to discredit the Negro race or to incite riot" and warned that labor could not afford to appear to encourage "lawlessness and racial strife." No other Black newspaper in the search window was found to have reported the circular.

accounts.label: Teamsters' Local 211 circular
accounts.gist: Claimed on 'reliable information' that a carload of Negroes was being imported from East St. Louis to break the strike, and urged citizens to protect their families and homes.

accounts.label: Monitor editorial
accounts.gist: Said it had traced the report, that it was 'absolutely false' and manufactured for a purpose, and that no Black strikebreakers were being brought to Omaha.

framing.detail: The Monitor called the circular propaganda meant to create prejudice against the Colored race and warned that organized labor could not afford to encourage 'lawlessness and racial strife', while declaring itself not opposed to organized labor.

versions.value: A carload of Negroes was being imported from East St. Louis to break the strike (union circular)
No Negro strikebreakers were being imported; the report was manufactured (Monitor)

conflicts.note: Both versions come from the same editorial, which reprints the circular and rebuts it; the Monitor says it traced the report down.

record_check.record: The circular text is cut off.
record_check.dossier: The circular is reprinted in full, ending with 'Prettiest Mile Revolver club, take notice!' and the signature of the union's conference committee.
Only a circular is reported (with an appeal to a revolver club); no gathering of armed men or other act is described. 'threat' at most.
One article (A2); the other Monitor item on the same page (A1) is not about the strike.
The circular targeted Black people generally (alleged Black strikebreakers); no individual victims.

info: Circular in circulation during the teamsters' strike, reported in the Monitor of June 19, 1919
Circular claimed a carload of Negroes was being imported from East St. Louis to break the strike
Teamsters' Local No. 211 ('Conference Committee Teamsters' Union, Local 211')

sources.note: Editorial reprinting Teamsters' Local No. 211 circular 'Warning to Citizens!' and calling its report of imported Black strikebreakers false.
quotes: What concerns us now especially is the propaganda being spread by Teamsters' Local No. 211, by means of circulars evidently intended to create prejudice against the Colored race.
To protect their wives and daughters from the horrors of East St. Louis. To safeguard their homes, their valuables and their lives!
Prettiest Mile Revolver club, take notice!
There are no Negro strike breakers being imported into Omaha and Mr. Rooney of the Teamsters' Union knows it.
It cannot afford to appear in the attitude of encouraging lawlessness and racial strife.

set_aside: Masthead and editorial on Black leadership and the NAACP; does not mention the strike or the circular.
Report of the NAACP conference in Cleveland; mentions an Omaha minister presiding at a session but not the strike.
